concepts.name: Literal character matching
concepts.summary: Recognise that most characters in a pattern match themselves and that a pattern is searched for within a string.

concepts.name: Metacharacters and escaping
concepts.summary: Explain which characters have special meaning and use a backslash to match them literally.

concepts.name: Dot wildcard
concepts.summary: Understand that the dot matches any single character except usually a newline.

concepts.name: Character classes
concepts.summary: Read and explain sets like [abc], ranges like [a-z] and negated sets like [^0-9] as matching one character from a set.

concepts.name: Shorthand classes
concepts.summary: Recall that \d, \w and \s match digits, word characters and whitespace and that uppercase versions negate them.

concepts.name: Basic quantifiers
concepts.summary: Explain how *, + and ? repeat the preceding item zero or more, one or more, or zero or one times.

concepts.name: Match versus no match
concepts.summary: Interpret whether a pattern finds a match in a sample string and which part of the text was matched.

misconceptions.text: A regular expression is the same as a shell glob, so * means any characters on its own.
A pattern must match the whole string to be considered a match.
Inside square brackets, [abc] matches the sequence abc.

concepts.name: Anchors
concepts.summary: Use ^ and $ to tie a pattern to the start and end of a string or line so it validates whole input.

concepts.name: Word boundaries
concepts.summary: Use \b to match whole words rather than substrings.

concepts.name: Capturing groups
concepts.summary: Group parts of a pattern with parentheses to apply quantifiers to them and to extract the matched text.

concepts.name: Alternation
concepts.summary: Use | to match one of several alternatives and understand its low precedence.

concepts.name: Counted quantifiers
concepts.summary: Use {n}, {n,} and {n,m} to specify exact or bounded repetition counts.

concepts.name: Replacement with backreferences
concepts.summary: Rewrite text by inserting captured groups into a replacement string.

concepts.name: Regex flags
concepts.summary: Explain how flags such as case-insensitive, global and multiline change matching behaviour.

misconceptions.text: The pattern cat|dog anchored as ^cat|dog$ requires the whole string to be cat or dog.
Without the global flag a replace changes every occurrence.
^ and $ always match the start and end of each line.

concepts.name: Greedy versus lazy quantifiers
concepts.summary: Analyse how greedy quantifiers take as much as possible and use lazy forms like *? to match the shortest span.

concepts.name: Non-capturing and named groups
concepts.summary: Choose non-capturing groups for grouping only and named groups to make extraction readable.

concepts.name: Backreferences in patterns
concepts.summary: Match repeated text such as doubled words by referring back to an earlier group inside the pattern.

concepts.name: Lookahead and lookbehind
concepts.summary: Use positive and negative lookarounds to require or forbid context without consuming it.

concepts.name: Matching engine API usage
concepts.summary: Choose between full match, search, find-all, split and replace operations in a language's regex library.

concepts.name: Decomposing a pattern
concepts.summary: Break a complex pattern into parts and test it against matching and non-matching samples to locate faults.

concepts.name: Multiline and dotall modes
concepts.summary: Analyse how multiline and dotall modes change anchors and the dot when matching across lines.

misconceptions.text: Lookaheads consume characters and so appear in the matched text.
A lazy quantifier finds the best or shortest match overall rather than the shortest from the current start position.
Parentheses are only for grouping and have no effect on the captured results.

concepts.name: Backtracking behaviour
concepts.summary: Analyse how a backtracking engine tries alternatives and why match order and quantifier choice affect results and speed.

concepts.name: Catastrophic backtracking
concepts.summary: Evaluate patterns with nested or overlapping quantifiers for exponential-time risk and judge their danger on untrusted input.

concepts.name: Possessive quantifiers and atomic groups
concepts.summary: Use possessive and atomic constructs to prevent needless backtracking and understand when they change results.

concepts.name: Unicode-aware matching
concepts.summary: Analyse how encodings, normalisation, and property classes like \p{L} affect what \w, case folding and the dot match.

concepts.name: Engine flavour differences
concepts.summary: Evaluate how dialects differ in supported syntax and semantics and judge portability of a pattern.

concepts.name: Regex versus parser choice
concepts.summary: Judge when regex is the right tool and when nested or context-sensitive formats such as HTML require a real parser.

concepts.name: Validation pattern design
concepts.summary: Evaluate validation patterns for false positives and negatives, such as emails and dates, and decide how strict to be.

misconceptions.text: Regex can reliably parse arbitrary nested HTML or balanced brackets.
All regex engines run in linear time regardless of pattern.
A single regex can fully validate an email address according to the specification.

concepts.name: Automata theory foundations
concepts.summary: Evaluate regex features against finite automata, explaining which constructs keep a language regular and which exceed it.

concepts.name: Linear-time engine trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge when to choose non-backtracking engines for guaranteed performance and what features such engines give up.

concepts.name: ReDoS-resistant pattern design
concepts.summary: Design patterns and surrounding controls such as timeouts and input limits that keep untrusted-input matching safe.

concepts.name: Regex-based tokenizer design
concepts.summary: Create a tokenizer from ordered regex rules, handling longest-match and priority conflicts.

concepts.name: Maintainable regex architecture
concepts.summary: Create patterns that are composed, commented, tested and documented so teams can maintain them.

concepts.name: Large-scale text transformation strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches to bulk searching and rewriting, weighing regex, structured parsing and tooling for correctness and speed.

concepts.name: Regex test strategy
concepts.summary: Create test suites with adversarial, boundary and fuzzed inputs that expose false matches and performance faults.

misconceptions.text: Modern regex with backreferences and lookarounds still describes only regular languages.
Switching to a linear-time engine lets you keep every feature, including backreferences.
Tests that pass on typical inputs show a pattern is safe.
